# Two Methods, Two Estimates for the 1906 Earthquake

Two approaches have produced different estimates of the 1906 earthquake’s magnitude: a seismic analysis suggested 7.7, while a USGS team’s re-evaluation of geodetic measurements estimated 7.9.

The seismic analysis examined recordings from 96 observatories. It digitized and modeled usable data from 12, suggesting a surface-wave magnitude of 7.7.

The USGS team took a different approach, re-evaluating geodetic measurements made before and after the earthquake. These measurements captured ground deformation through angles and distances between benchmarks, producing an estimate of 7.9.

The estimates come from different kinds of measurements, and methods of assessing earthquake size can yield different results.
